mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Process each "X gives N to Y" statement in the order it appears, immediately subtracting N from X and adding N to Y, because later statements refer to the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer statement is encountered while reading the narrative.
mathgap.example: Applying a later transfer using the original counts of the giver, ignoring earlier transfers.

mathgap.title: Signed Interpretation of "has K more than"
mathgap.principle: A statement "A has K more than B" translates to A − B = K, i.e. A = B + K. Do not swap the order.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a comparative statement of the form "A has K more than B".
mathgap.example: Interpreting "A has K more than B" as B = A + K.

mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: For a sentence like "The number of potatoes that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of potatoes that C and D have" translate to (A − B) = (C − D). Preserve the order on both sides.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing a comparison‑transfer equality that equates a "has more than" difference to another difference.
mathgap.example: Treating the right‑hand side as |C − D| or swapping C and D.

mathgap.title: Signed Interpretation of "difference between X and Y"
mathgap.principle: The phrase "difference between the number of X and Y" should be read as X − Y, preserving the order, not as an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement mentions the "difference between" two quantities.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "difference between X and Y" as |X − Y|.

mathgap.title: Current‑Count Constraint for "has N"
mathgap.principle: A statement "A has N potatoes" constrains A’s count at that point in the narrative, i.e. after any earlier transfers or constraints, not just the initial count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a direct count statement.
mathgap.example: Treating "A has N" as the initial count and ignoring earlier transfers that changed A’s amount.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable’s value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations and recompute any newly solvable variables, iterating until no further deductions are possible.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving any equation that yields a concrete value.
mathgap.example: Failing to substitute a newly known variable into other equations, leaving them unsolved.

mathgap.title: Allow Negative Differences in Contradictory "more than" Phrases
mathgap.principle: When a "more than" phrase appears on the left side of an equality that contradicts a previous comparison, allow the difference to be negative rather than forcing it to be positive.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a "has K more than" statement yields a negative K due to other constraints.
mathgap.example: Rejecting a solution because a derived "has K more than" gave a negative K, assuming it must be positive.

mathgap.title: Consistency Check After Solving
mathgap.principle: After obtaining values for all variables, verify each original statement—including transfers, direct counts, and difference equations—to ensure the solution satisfies the entire narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the system and before outputting the answer.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution without checking that it satisfies a later "has K more than" statement.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: When processing any comparative statement (e.g., "A has K more than B" or "the number of X that A has more than B equals the difference between C and D"), use the current counts of the referenced persons at that point in the narrative, after all earlier transfers and constraints have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: During a sequential pass through the problem text, for each comparative statement.
mathgap.example: Treating a later "A has K more than B" as if it referred to the initial counts, ignoring earlier transfers that changed A or B.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the subset of equations that involve the queried person directly or through a chain of dependencies, and solve only this subsystem, ignoring unrelated equations that cannot affect the answer.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving, after parsing all statements, when the goal is to find a single person's count.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve for the queried person's count by including equations about unrelated persons, leading to contradictions or unnecessary complexity.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in "has K more than" statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often misinterprets the phrase, assuming the relationship is B = A + K instead of A = B + K.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always translate "A has K more than B" to A − B = K (i.e., A = B + K) and keep the order as written.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes "difference between X and Y" means |X − Y|, losing sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order: interpret "difference between X and Y" as X − Y, not as an absolute value.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies all transfers simultaneously or out of order, forgetting that later statements refer to updated counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfer statements in the exact order they appear, updating counts after each.

mathgap.description: Treating "has N" as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes "A has N" sets the initial value of A, ignoring earlier transfers that may have altered A's count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "A has N" as a constraint on A's current count at that point in the narrative.

mathgap.description: Assuming all "more than" differences must be positive
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model expects K > 0 in "A has K more than B", rejecting negative differences that arise from other constraints.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Allow K to be negative when required by other equations; do not enforce positivity unless explicitly stated.
